_readme: Independent probes behind the Fidelity Index (site/AI-HANDOFF.md §3.4). A probe starts from frames published by third parties (lists of organizations, or of meetings) and reads each organizer's own events page without looking at the Runway. It counts the distinct qualifying dated meetings found in its window and how many of them the Runway already held; the Fidelity Index is held ÷ found for the latest probe. 'history' records the same count for sources brought up before the first probe. 'finished' is the UTC time the probe's comparison with the Runway was recorded; the header's Horizon scan stamp shows it. 'reconciliation' follows the meetings the probe found that the Runway lacked ('missing' = found - held): each is added to the Runway, rejected with a reason, or still open; the Horizon scan dot is green when none is open and yellow while any is. For the first probe it was read afterwards from the modification time of that result file. Add each new probe with its date and finish time; never remove one. The organization lists and the meetings found are kept with the curator's working files; every meeting a probe finds that the Runway lacks enters review.

reconciliation.note: Added on 2026-09-26: Charter Oak Conference 2027 and NCAPA Annual Summer Conference 2027. The other 35 meetings the probe found await review.

probes.method: Seven frames published by third parties: six lists of organizations, sampled by a fixed rule (every organization, or every second or third name in alphabetical order), and independent editorial lists of NP conferences. Each selected organizer's own events page was read without the Runway's data. A meeting qualifies if it is a dated conference, symposium or summit for APPs starting in the window; advocacy days, short courses, business meetings and meetings of unclear relevance to APPs are left out, as are three items read through a relay against the Runway's reading rules. Run by AI agents under the curator's direction.
